Text runs from the top to the last line, with a centred italic title above the second paragraph. Catchword at the lower right. Narrow fragments at the left and right edges belong to the neighbouring page and are not transcribed.

main_text.p: re occasionem populo dedisse ferociendi ac tumultuandi contra reges proximè secutos, si quid violentius pro imperio viderentur agere, & turbulentos quoque motus inter sese ciendi, excussa legum & imperii reverentia; atque in hujusmodi tumultu, dum dirimendi ejus ergo accurreret, regem Eunomium, Eurypontis nepotem, Lycurgi legum-latoris celeberrimi patrem, accepto vul-nere mortem oppetiisse.

head.i: Lycurgus reformando statui confuso & fluctuanti legislator creatus.

main_text.p: CVm vero confusio hæc cum tempore crefceret, & status regni incertus fluctuaret, cum populus à regibus, reges à populo sibi metuerent, & cum alii in populo rebus turbatis opes cumulassent, & possessiones soli fere omnes in se vertissent, alii contra, & hi numero plurimi, rerum inopiâ premerentur, ac rixarentur cum fortuna sua, & horum fremitum divites formidarent, viderenturque hæc majus malum, adeoque regni interitum portendere; à Lycurgo, oportunè tum ex longa peregrinatione domum reverso, medendis his malis & constituendæ melius reipublicæ manus admota fuit. Erat quippe Lycurgus è regio sanguine vir

page.notes: Printing: the title "Lycurgus reformando statui..." is in italic, and the body reads "status" (the title spelling "statui" is as printed). The large initial "C" of "CVm" is set as one word. Fragments of text at the left edge ("tua", "ngr") and small marks at the right edge are from the neighbouring page and were not transcribed. Faint marks at the bottom left are not legible text. The catchword "vir" is at the lower right.
